work.title: Designed, validated, industrialized.
work.description: Product development and mechanical design work — open any card for challenge, contribution, and outcome.

elaraby-appliance.title: Home Appliance Component Development
elaraby-appliance.hook: Appliance parts that have to pass mold, assembly, and the quality gate — not just look right in CAD.
elaraby-appliance.challenge: Lead design and development of home appliance components and assemblies under production schedules, balancing performance, cost, and manufacturability for injection-molded and sheet-metal parts.
elaraby-appliance.work: Create and refine 3D models in CATIA and 3DExperience. Define subsystem structures, manage engineering BOM through the lifecycle, build prototypes, run test activities, and iterate with R&D, production, quality, procurement, and suppliers.
elaraby-appliance.result: Production-bound designs with documented EBOMs, technical reports, and compliance with company and international standards. Supports industrialization and localization initiatives at ELARABY Group.

mold-injection.title: Injection-Molded Appliance Housing
mold-injection.hook: A plastic part family that has to mold cleanly, assemble fast, and survive the appliance lifecycle.
mold-injection.challenge: Design injection-molded components with correct draft, wall thickness, and ribbing while meeting structural and aesthetic requirements for a high-volume appliance line.
mold-injection.work: Applied DFM/DFA principles, material selection, and tolerance analysis. Coordinated with tooling and production teams on moldability feedback and design revisions before release.
mold-injection.result: Validated mold-ready geometry with improved manufacturability and fewer late-stage tooling surprises.

sheet-metal-bracket.title: Sheet-Metal Bracket & Enclosure Family
sheet-metal-bracket.hook: Brackets that have to bend, punch, and assemble without fighting the line.
sheet-metal-bracket.challenge: Develop sheet-metal parts that meet stiffness targets, fit existing assembly interfaces, and remain economical at volume.
sheet-metal-bracket.work: Detailed sheet-metal designs with bend allowances, hole patterns, and GD&T. Supported prototype builds and fit checks with production and quality teams.
sheet-metal-bracket.result: Released sheet-metal designs with clear tolerances and assembly documentation for repeatable manufacturing.

prototype-validation.title: Prototype Build & Test Loop
prototype-validation.hook: Build it, break it, fix it — before the factory does.
prototype-validation.challenge: Verify mechanical performance and assembly fit early enough to change the design cheaply, not after tooling is committed.
prototype-validation.work: Built and evaluated prototypes, captured performance data, ran root-cause investigations, and fed improvements back into CAD and EBOM releases.
prototype-validation.result: Fewer late engineering changes and clearer evidence behind design decisions before handover to production.

ebom-lifecycle.title: EBOM & Engineering Change Management
ebom-lifecycle.hook: The drawing is only half the product — the BOM has to stay true as the program moves.
ebom-lifecycle.challenge: Keep engineering structures, specifications, and change records aligned as designs evolve through prototype, pilot, and production phases.
ebom-lifecycle.work: Managed EBOM structures in SAP-linked workflows, prepared drawings and specifications, and supported engineering change management with cross-functional teams.
ebom-lifecycle.result: Traceable product data from development through release, with documentation suitable for audit and supplier coordination.
ebom-lifecycle.alt: Engineering BOM and product data management

supplier-dfm.title: Supplier Development & Cost Optimization
supplier-dfm.hook: When the supplier says the part is hard to make, the answer is in the model — not in a meeting.
supplier-dfm.challenge: Improve manufacturability and cost while protecting critical functions and compliance requirements during supplier engagement and localization work.
supplier-dfm.work: Ran DFMEA and design reviews, supported supplier development, and applied tolerance and material changes with documented validation.
supplier-dfm.result: Design updates that reduced manufacturing risk and supported cost and localization goals without silent spec drift.

asuwind-turbine.title: Compact Wind Turbine Generator — ASUWind
asuwind-turbine.hook: A small-scale generator designed to compete on efficiency, not just on slides.
asuwind-turbine.challenge: Contribute to the mechanical design of a compact wind turbine generator as part of a university team targeting competitive small-scale power generation.
asuwind-turbine.work: Supported design and development of mechanical subsystems, coordinated with team members on integration, prototyping, and test preparation at ASUWind.
asuwind-turbine.result: Contributed to a cohesive mechanical design direction for a competitive small-scale wind energy prototype.
asuwind-turbine.alt: ASUWind compact wind turbine mechanical design

tolerance-stack.title: Tolerance Stack & GD&T Reviews
tolerance-stack.hook: When assemblies fail fit at the line, the stack-up usually tells the story.
tolerance-stack.challenge: Ensure critical interfaces close across multiple parts and suppliers without over-constraining the design or hiding risk in average dimensions.
tolerance-stack.work: Applied GD&T, ran tolerance analyses, and documented design reviews with production and quality stakeholders before release.
tolerance-stack.result: Clearer control of critical characteristics and fewer fit issues discovered only at assembly.

sap-workflow.title: SAP-Linked Engineering Documentation
sap-workflow.hook: If the BOM in SAP and the model in CAD disagree, production picks the expensive truth.
sap-workflow.challenge: Maintain consistent engineering data across CAD releases, BOM structures, and shop-facing documentation.
sap-workflow.work: Used SAP with Excel/VBA and structured reporting to improve engineering workflows, product data accuracy, and decision support for the team.
sap-workflow.result: More reliable handoffs between design, documentation, and production planning.

3dexperience-architecture.title: 3DExperience Product Architecture
3dexperience-architecture.hook: A product line needs a structure — not a folder full of parts with similar names.
3dexperience-architecture.challenge: Define subsystem structures and design architectures that scale as variants and engineering changes accumulate.
3dexperience-architecture.work: Built product architectures in 3DExperience, linked components to EBOM intent, and kept models organized for cross-team collaboration.
3dexperience-architecture.result: Clearer product breakdown and faster navigation for engineers joining mid-program.

supply-chain-sc4x.title: Supply Chain Technology Exposure — SC4x
supply-chain-sc4x.hook: Engineering decisions echo in the supply chain — seeing that loop makes better designs.
supply-chain-sc4x.challenge: Connect mechanical product thinking with supply-chain and data concepts through structured learning and practical tooling exposure.
supply-chain-sc4x.work: Participated in supply-chain technology programs, including hands-on work with data-oriented tooling and machine-learning concepts applied to logistics problems.
supply-chain-sc4x.result: Broader view of how design choices affect downstream planning, cost, and delivery — useful when industrializing appliance programs.

capstone-energy.title: University Capstone — Energy Systems
capstone-energy.hook: Graduation work that had to prove itself on a bench, not just in a report.
capstone-energy.challenge: Deliver a rigorous mechanical engineering capstone within university standards while meeting real performance and documentation expectations.
capstone-energy.work: Applied mechanical design and production engineering fundamentals from Ain Shams University coursework to a structured graduation project with formal review and documentation.
capstone-energy.result: Completed B.Sc. requirements in Mechanical Design & Production Engineering with hands-on design and analysis experience.

about.title: I work where design meets the factory.
paragraphs: I am a Product Development Engineer at ELARABY Group and a mechanical design engineer with a B.Sc. from Ain Shams University. My work sits where CAD, EBOM, prototyping, and production requirements all have to align for home appliance programs.

Before ELARABY, I contributed as a Mechanical Design Engineer with ASUWind on compact wind turbine development. I collaborate daily with R&D, production, quality, procurement, and suppliers — and I care about documentation, GD&T, DFMEA, and SAP-linked data that teams can actually use.

challenge.launchBody: Three product-development dilemmas from real program pressure. Your answers show how you think.

rounds.question: The tolerance stack fails at assembly, but the launch date is fixed. What do you do first?

options.label: Loosen every tolerance on the bracket family.
options.title: Fast paperwork, fuzzy control.
options.feedback: Blanket tolerance relaxation often hides the true driver and invites repeat failures at the line.

options.label: Measure the stack, identify the critical contributor, and propose a targeted fix.
options.title: Evidence before ECO.
options.feedback: A focused stack-up analysis gives production and quality a fix they can verify — not just hope for.

options.label: Ship as-is and sort at final inspection.
options.title: Speed today, rework tomorrow.
options.feedback: Late sorting is expensive and rarely catches functional risk — only obvious fit issues.

rounds.question: Tooling lead time slips, but marketing locked the launch. What is your next move?

options.label: Freeze CAD and hope the mold catches up.
options.title: Frozen design, moving deadline.
options.feedback: A freeze without supplier feedback can lock in moldability problems that surface too late.

options.label: Run a DFM review with tooling and propose a simplified interim geometry.
options.title: Design for what can ship.
options.feedback: Interim solutions with clear ECO paths protect the date without pretending risk does not exist.

options.label: Reopen every part in the assembly for a full redesign.
options.title: Correct, but not on this calendar.
options.feedback: Full redesign may be right technically but fails the schedule constraint — scope the minimum viable change.

rounds.question: Marketing adds a feature after EBOM release. What changes first?

options.label: Update the model quietly and skip formal change control.
options.title: Invisible change, visible pain later.
options.feedback: Undocumented changes break SAP, suppliers, and quality traceability — especially at volume.

options.label: Impact analysis, ECO, and aligned updates to CAD, BOM, and drawings.
options.title: Change control is part of the product.
options.feedback: Formal ECO with cross-functional sign-off keeps production and suppliers on the same revision.

options.label: Reject the change outright without analysis.
options.title: Safe default, weak partnership.
options.feedback: Sometimes the right answer is no — but it should follow impact data, not reflex.

high.title: Release saved — systems thinker.
high.text: You balanced schedule pressure with manufacturability, data discipline, and cost awareness. That is the product-development loop I use on appliance programs at ELARABY.

fast.title: Fast mover, exposed validation.
fast.text: You kept momentum high, but the program carries hidden technical debt. Add earlier stack-up checks and supplier DFM before locking EBOM.

default.title: Release recovered — one more validation pass.
default.text: The engineering direction is sound. Strengthen acceptance criteria and change control before calling it ready for production.
